text:
sandeep: quick one — we're seeing a patient app consume burst credits and then get slammed by preemption when reserved capacity is tight. want to sanity-check a policy sketch before i turn it into an RFC.

owen: can you summarize the observable sequence? curious where backpressure is missing.

sandeep: sequence: tenant has small soft reservation + burst credits; sudden traffic spike => autoscaler accepts more jobs into burst lane; later global contention => preemption evicts burst pods first; client sees many 503s and retries, burning more credits and amplifying the problem.

maria: that sounds like classic positive feedback loop. do we have metrics showing retry amplification vs initial request volume?

sandeep: yeah, SLO dashboard shows token cost + request rate spiking after the first evictions. retry multiplier ~2.3x for that tenant in the 10m window.

rachel: two parts to solve: admission/backpressure at the gateway and a credit-exhaustion policy that avoids making retries worse. ie, fail-fast vs queue.

owen: I like fail-fast if the tenant is already being preempted, but that hurts UX. maybe a short queue + jittered backoff hint header? header would let apps adapt.

sandeep: propose hybrid: when burst credits available -> allow admission up to N concurrent bursts. when credits exhausted or pool headroom < threshold -> instead of immediate eviction we offer a 1s-5s soft-queue token with Retry-After and X-Redwood-Admission: queued. If queue timeout, return 429 with structured hint.

maria: what about cost shaping — we can't let long queues occupy GPU resources. queue must be in the proxy layer (no GPU allocation) so we don't tie up resources.

sandeep: agreed — queue in proxy/edge; only admit to GPU when slot free. also: when preemption happens, reclaim bursts but do not immediately refill from queue; apply cooldown per-tenant to avoid thundering herd.

rachel: how do preemptible credits interact? do credits reset on retry? that could be exploited.

sandeep: credits should be consumed on admission, not on completion. so a retry that never got admitted doesn't burn credits. but if a request timed out after GPU allocation, it consumed credits.

owen: nice. we also need a visibility signal: admit decisions should emit events to the console and a per-tenant metric like admission_state{allowed,queued,rejected} so we can alert on queue growth.

infra-bot: deployment reminder: any change touching proxy admission needs feature-flag gate + canary. See deploy-checklist: https://intra.redwood/infra/deploy-checklist

maria: possible policy sketch (pseudo-yaml):
```
admission_policy:
  burst_window: 60s
  burst_max_concurrent: 8
  credit_consumption: on_admit
  proxy_queue:
    enabled: true
    max_depth: 50
    max_latency: 5s
    per_tenant_cooldown_after_reject: 10s
  preemption:
    eviction_order: [burst, on_demand]
    post_eviction_cooldown: 30s
  telemetry:
    emit_counters: [allowed, queued, rejected, evicted]
```

rachel: minor tweak — add a pool_headroom_gate %; if headroom < 12% then move to strict reject mode (no queue) to preserve SLA for reserved tenants.

sandeep: good call. also propose cost-shaping knob that reduces allowed concurrency proportionally when monthly spend > committed budget for tenant.

owen: tradeoffs: more complexity in proxy, more knobs to tune, but avoids burn-and-evict cascade. sounds like a reasonable staged roll out: start with telemetry-only + feature flag, then queue, then cooldowns.

maria: agree. action items?

sandeep: I'll draft an RFC w/ API changes for Retry-After header and X-Redwood-Admission values, include the pseudo-yaml, and a runbook for when a tenant hits repeated eviction loops. plan: telemetry-only PR this week, queue behind flag next sprint.

rachel: +1. add e2e tests that simulate retry amplification.

owen: tagging you @rachel and @maria for review.

sandeep: thanks all. will ping when RFC is up.
